text:
Irene Choi: quick heads up for runtime profile pack work — fleet is not as “single baseline” as we’d like rn. sharing the driver/CUDA spread we’re seeing + what I think needs to go into compatibility checks.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1, I pulled numbers from the last 7d inventory snapshot. tl;dr: H100 is mostly converged, L40S is messy, B200 bring-up is going to be *very* gated.

Irene Choi: current spread (hosted + dedicated combined; private obviously unknown):
- H100 SXM (majority): driver 550.54.14 w/ CUDA 12.4 runtime image (most), some still on 545.29.06 (CUDA 12.2 image)
- H100 PCIe (smaller pools): more variance; a few nodes still on 535.x (older AMI path)
- L40S: widest spread. driver 535.129 / 545.29 / 550.54 all present. CUDA runtime images vary 12.1/12.2/12.4 depending on the cluster.
- MIG: H100 MIG is enabled only in 2 small hosted regions (for bursty embeddings). everywhere else MIG disabled. L40S no MIG.
- NCCL/CUDNN versions also differ between images, but driver/CUDA is the big one for kernel selection + stability.

Vanessa Ortiz: adding a couple gotchas:
- some “H100” pools are mixed PCIe vs SXM (same customer SKU label but different perf). we *try* to keep separate but there are a couple legacy pools that are mixed.
- on L40S we have both 48GB and 46GB usable memory depending on reserved carve-outs (monitoring agents + hugepages config). shows up as ~1.5–2GB swing in headroom.

Neha Kapoor: what we need from runtime team is a hard stance: do profiles require a min driver/CUDA? and what happens when we’re below it?

Yuki Sato: for kernel pack we’re already seeing certain attention variants are only safe on >= 550 + CUDA 12.4 (esp for the v3 kernels). on older combos we can run but we either (a) force fallback kernel set or (b) refuse to start w/ that profile.

Quentin Harris: this maps pretty directly to the “compatibility matrix” idea. recommendation:
1) profile manifest should include explicit `min_driver`, `min_cuda_runtime` per (sku, kernel_set)
2) runtime selection should match on sku + driver range + cuda runtime range
3) if no match, selection returns “baseline-safe” profile (or fails, depending on deployment mode)

Ethan Park: + control plane override story: hosted can auto-select safest available. dedicated/private need deterministic behavior: if customer pins profile_version, we should error loudly when incompatible (so they don’t think they’re running v1.2 but actually falling back silently).

Irene Choi: exactly. the infra side of this is: we can’t guarantee the whole fleet flips driver in lockstep. we have rolling AMI/image updates, and some dedicated tenants are intentionally frozen.

Vanessa Ortiz: real numbers from snapshot (approx):
- H100 nodes: ~78% on 550.54, ~18% on 545.29, ~4% on 535.x (mostly PCIe)
- L40S nodes: ~41% on 550.54, ~37% on 545.29, ~22% on 535.x
(yes we are working on converging L40S; it’s just slower b/c those clusters are older + more customer pinned)

Neha Kapoor: so compatibility checks need to cover:
- driver major/minor
- CUDA runtime image version
- MIG on/off (or MIG profile)
- PCIe vs SXM (or at least memory bw class)
- memory headroom carve-outs?? (not sure if that’s runtime-visible)

Yuki Sato: runtime can reliably detect:
- `nvidia-smi` driver version
- GPU name + pci device id (SXM vs PCIe is detectable)
- MIG mode + MIG instances
- total memory
CUDA runtime version is trickier; depends on container. but we can log `cudaRuntimeGetVersion()` and/or `nvcc --version` equivalent if present.

Quentin Harris: I’d avoid depending on “nvcc exists” in prod images. `cudaRuntimeGetVersion()` is probably the least janky. also, profile pack should key on “runtime ABI” not “toolkit installed”.

Ethan Park: for hosted/dedicated, control plane knows the runtime image tag and can pass that to runtime as a label. private installer can do detection at install-time but also pass through as config.

Irene Choi: from infra POV, I want two things:
A) strict mode for B200: if driver/CUDA isn’t exactly on the supported list, runtime should refuse to enable the profile (and ideally refuse to start inference unless explicitly `--allow_unsupported=true`)
B) warn-only mode for legacy L40S/H100 pools: log + metric when we’re not on the “preferred” combo, but still run on a safe fallback kernel set.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1 on strict B200. we already expect B200 driver baseline to be 555+ (TBD) and CUDA 12.4+ only. early nodes are all over the place.

Yuki Sato: kernel behavior observed:
- on driver 535, kernel fallback rates spike (we see PTX->SASS mismatches / compile paths) + occasional perf cliffs
- on 545, mostly ok but v3 kernels not always selected due to missing capabilities
- on 550 + CUDA 12.4, stable and best perf
so the profile should encode “if < 550 then force kernel_set=v2” kind of rule.

Neha Kapoor: can we do something like “profile requires capabilities rather than versions”? e.g., query for specific feature support.

Quentin Harris: we can do capabilities checks for some things, but versions are still the easiest guardrail. capabilities detection tends to become “if this function returns X on this driver but Y on another”. I’d still encode min versions + allow runtime to choose safer kernel set when below.

Ethan Park: also have to think about deterministic debugging. if SRE sees `profile_id=h100-default` but kernel_set differs due to driver, that’s confusing unless we explicitly surface `kernel_set_selected` + `compatibility_reason` in logs/metrics.

Irene Choi: yes please. also callout: instance type mapping is not always 1:1 with SKU label. some clouds are weird with “H100-80GB” but actually different host configs. we’ll feed you the mapping doc separately, but profile selection can’t assume instance_type => exact perf.

FleetBot: inventory note: cluster=l40s-us-east-1a has 13 nodes pending image upgrade (driver 535.129.03 -> 550.54.15). ETA 10d.

Vanessa Ortiz: another edge: PCIe H100 nodes often have lower CPU headroom / different NUMA. if profile pack starts requiring host-level pinning (hugepages/numa), that will vary by cluster. needs to be “best-effort” not “required” unless we control it.

Yuki Sato: got it. we’ll keep host-level knobs in a separate section and only enforce in hosted where runtime has confidence.

Neha Kapoor: action items I’m hearing:
- Infra will provide: “supported driver/CUDA baselines per SKU” and “known exceptions windows”
- Runtime will implement: compatibility gating w/ three states: compatible / compatible-with-fallback / incompatible
- Metrics: count nodes running fallback due to driver/CUDA mismatch (by sku, region)

Quentin Harris: + specify behavior by deployment mode:
- Hosted: auto-select best compatible profile; fallback allowed; alert when fallback % > threshold
- Dedicated: default is stable baseline; allow customer pin; if pinned profile incompatible => fail fast + clear error; optional “force fallback” flag for support
- Private: installer warns + runtime warns; by default, fail fast only for “known-unsafe” combinations (we should maintain a denylist)

Irene Choi: sounds right. I’ll write up a quick matrix and send to @Yuki Sato / @Quentin Harris so you can encode it in the schema.

Vanessa Ortiz: please also include MIG nuance. profiles should treat MIG as separate sku-ish. H100 1g.10gb vs 7g.80gb etc. we should not accidentally apply the “full GPU” profile to MIG slice.

Yuki Sato: yep. we’ll treat MIG mode as part of the selection key. if MIG detected and profile doesn’t declare MIG support, we’ll refuse to load it.

Neha Kapoor: cool. let’s sync w/ SRE later this week so rollout gates include “fallback rate” + “incompatible nodes” dashboards.

Irene Choi: :thumbsup: I’ll post the inventory snippet + baseline proposal in this thread once cleaned up.
